actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

dimensions.assessment: Affects rural communities, states, Indian Tribes, tribal organizations, and entities receiving grants for substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery services.
dimensions.evidence: maintain a program to be known as the Rural Communities Opioid Response Program to establish and expand prevention, treatment, and recovery services in rural areas

dimensions.assessment: Supports the continuation and expansion of grant-funded delivery models and technical assistance for rural substance use disorder services.
dimensions.evidence: An eligible entity that receives a grant or cooperative agreement under this section may use funds... to provide direct prevention, treatment, and recovery services

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $165,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to fund grants and cooperative agreements.
dimensions.evidence: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $165,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act to establish a statutory authorization for the RCORP program and set eligibility, grant periods, and permitted uses of funds.
dimensions.evidence: Subpart I of part D of title III of the Public Health Service Act is amended by inserting after section 330A-2... SEC. 330A-3. RURAL COMMUNITIES OPIOID RESPONSE PROGRAM.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations and grant activities over a five-year period from fiscal years 2026 through 2030, with individual grants lasting up to 5 years.
dimensions.evidence: appropriated to carry out this section $165,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

missing_information: Actual funding levels appropriated by future legislation are not predetermined beyond the authorization amount.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Public Health Service Act to formally authorize and maintain the Rural Communities Opioid Response Program (RCORP) through the Health Resources and Services Administration, authorizing $165,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
